The only favorable feature is QED, which is slightly higher in the neighbor, 0.8179 versus 0.7918 (delta -0.0261), so the query is a bit lower on this composite drug-likeness score. QED is also slightly lower in the query, 0.7918 versus 0.7968 (delta -0.005), which is a very small disadvantage. Neighbor 6 is the most nuanced negative-bioavailability analog, and it is the main counterweight in the set. But the query also has enolether once while the neighbor has none (delta +1), which is unfavorable. Even with those favorable shifts in ionizable-site count and TPSA, the enolether and higher logD differences remain important, so this neighbor does not overturn the overall concern about oral exposure. It is the clearest example of a negative neighbor where the query looks better on some composite properties but still carries structural and lipophilicity features that do not support a high-bioavailability interpretation.

Putting all six neighbors together, the three positive-bioavailability neighbors consistently highlight the query’s unfavorable enolether presence, higher topological polar surface area, higher logD, and more extreme partial-charge descriptors, with only QED and, in one case, neutral fraction offering partial relief.
